propositions: Full-suite scheduler load causes git-fetch dribble tests to intermittently fail stall detection despite passing in isolation, due to delayed Python fixture wake-ups reducing actual throughput below configured rate.

Test harness applies same 2-second artificial low-speed window to both zero-byte stall controls and above-floor dribble transfers, causing valid dribbling to be misclassified as stalled under scheduler delay.
Cumulative bytes-owed calculation alone cannot fix test flakes because libcurl aborts during uninterrupted scheduling gaps before catch-up pacing can compensate.

Production must retain 10-second low-speed window unchanged; test fix must separate fast 2-second window for zero-byte stall tests from production 10-second window for one real Git/libcurl dribble integration test.
